proposition.claim:
Definition 2.1 concerns a compact subgroup \(U\subset M(\widehat{\mathbb Z})\), with \(M\subset G\subset\operatorname{GL}_n\) connected reductive groups. The rational condition requires the appropriate connected Zariski closures, semisimplicity and centralizer equality. The residual condition is eventual and uniform in bounded index: for every fixed bound \(D\), a threshold \(M_U(D)\) controls all subgroups of the relevant residual image of index at most \(D\). It imposes no condition at every individual small prime.

The centralizer \(Z_G(M)\) is the full group scheme, not automatically its identity component. The abelianization \(M^{\mathrm{ab}}\), the full center \(Z(M)\), and the connected center are different objects. Likewise, stability under integral points \(G(\mathbb Z_p)\) is weaker than stability under the coaction of the integral group scheme \(G_{\mathbb Z_p}\). These distinctions are decisive in Problems 1, 2 and 4.

repair.content:
After excluding finitely many bad primes and divisors of the fixed component-group order, first form Y=G/F0, then X=Y/(F/F0). Averaging proves invariant base change; finite generation, torsion-free flatness and smooth geometric quotient fibers give smooth X and G->X. The normalization argument, with genuine coactions, gives integral X->orbit closure and the same integral-point criterion. Section6.3 then has identical convex zero sets and unchanged weight constants, with no additive constant.
